outcome: Not settled since 26 January 2024, but advanced in specific degrees and weights. Bolbachan (April 2024) proves the next-to-Milnor degree for all weights in characteristic zero. Kupers, Rudenko and Sierra (June 2026) prove a variant of the conjecture for weight 3 over arbitrary fields and, in August 2026, the variant of their Conjecture A.b for number fields in all weights; they state the variant matches Goncharov's Γ-statement literally only at weight 3. No AI system is named in any source found.
problem_asks: Read from the Wikipedia wording (“the cohomology of certain motivic complexes” coincides with “pieces of K-groups”), with the standard formulation used in Bolbachan's and Kupers–Rudenko–Sierra's papers filled in, because the January 2024 wording does not fix the degree range or coefficients. (1) For every field F and every weight n, the cohomology H^i of Goncharov's polylogarithmic motivic complex Γ(F,n), concentrated in degrees 1 ≤ i ≤ n, is rationally isomorphic to the weight-n motivic cohomology H^{i,n}_M(Spec F, Q); equivalently to the graded piece gr^n_γ K_{2n−i}(F)_Q of algebraic K-theory. (2) Parts asked, enumerated: (a) all fields F, of any characteristic; (b) all weights n; (c) every degree i with 1 ≤ i ≤ n. Known before the window: n ≤ 1; the top degree i = n in all weights (Milnor K-theory); and n = 2 (Suslin's description of the indecomposable K_3). Open in general, as far as the sources show, is every other (n, i) with n ≥ 3, i < n.

events.what_happened: Daniil Rudenko, “The Strong Suslin Reciprocity Law” (arXiv:1511.00520). Proves the strong Suslin reciprocity law conjectured by A. Goncharov, using a homotopy invariance theorem for the cohomology of polylogarithmic motivic complexes in the “next to Milnor” degree. Published as Compositio Math. 157 (2021) 649–676. A short Funktsional'nyi Analiz announcement appeared in 2016 (seen in a search snippet, not opened). Neighbouring Goncharov conjecture, pre-window; it is not a statement about H^i(Γ(F,n)) as such.
events.revisions: v1 2 Nov 2015; v2 10 Jul 2018; v3 22 Oct 2020 (current); journal reference Compositio Math. 157 (2021) 649–676, DOI 10.1112/S0010437X20007666.
events.delivers: Proves the strong Suslin reciprocity law, a different Goncharov conjecture (a contracting homotopy underlying Suslin reciprocity). Its ingredient is a homotopy-invariance statement for Γ-type cohomology in the next-to-Milnor degree. Does not state an isomorphism H^i(Γ(F,n)) ≅ H^{i,n}_M for any (n, i) beyond those already known.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: this is a neighbouring conjecture, not the cohomology statement.

events.what_happened: Alexander Goncharov and Daniil Rudenko, “Motivic correlators, cluster varieties and Zagier's conjecture on ζ_F(4)” (arXiv:1803.08585). Proves Zagier's conjecture for ζ_F(4) for number fields, and constructs canonical maps K_{8−i}(F)_Q → H^i(B•(F;4)) for i = 1..4 into the weight-4 polylogarithmic complex, which are isomorphisms for i = 4 by Suslin. The weight-4 Goncharov conjecture (the maps are isomorphisms in all degrees) is stated as Conjecture 1.4 and is not proved in the text read. Pre-window first posting; the fifth version (July 2026) is in-window and states acceptance by Annals of Mathematics.

events.what_happened: Steven Charlton, “Symmetries of weight 6 multiple polylogarithms and Goncharov's Depth Conjecture” (arXiv:2405.13853). Proves the higher-Zagier part of the weight-6, depth-3 reduction conjectured by Matveiakin and Rudenko, which together with their higher-Gangl part establishes Goncharov's Depth Conjecture in weight 6, depth 3. This is a different Goncharov conjecture, about multiple polylogarithms, not about H^i(Γ(F,n)). Ancillary Mathematica worksheets are used for verification (computer algebra, not AI).
events.revisions: v1 22 May 2024 only (5567 KB; comments: 70 pages, 3 figures, six ancillary files). Journal reference not given.
events.delivers: Goncharov's Depth Conjecture in weight 6, depth 3 only (with Matveiakin–Rudenko's higher-Gangl part, which the abstract says is formulated modulo the higher-Zagier part). No other weights, depths, or degrees; no statement about Γ(F,n) cohomology.
events.directly_checkable: Ancillary Mathematica worksheets (weight-4 and weight-6 verification files) are listed on the arXiv page, not opened.
events.direction: Proves a Goncharov conjecture (depth) in a restricted case, in the affirmative; no counterexample; neighbouring rather than on the cohomology statement.

events.what_happened: Vasily Bolbachan, “On the Goncharov's conjecture in degree m−1 and weight m” (arXiv:2404.06271; retitled “On Goncharov's conjecture in next to Milnor degree” in v2). For a field K of characteristic zero and m ≥ 2, Theorem 1.2 states H^{m−1,m}(Spec K, Q) ≅ H^{m−1}(Γ(K,m)) rationally, via a map 𝒯 that Theorem 1.3 calls a quasi-isomorphism, and an isomorphism when K is algebraically closed. The introduction says the full Goncharov conjecture (its Conjecture 1.1) was known only in very few cases before this paper; the author believes the result extends to positive characteristic but does not prove it. v2 corrects an earlier paper's argument: Lemma 2.16 of [Bol23] used a Lemma 2.14 whose proof was incorrect, and Lemma 2.14 is a special case of Lemma 3.7 proved here. The v1 comment notes text overlap with arXiv:2311.07567.
events.revisions: v1 9 Apr 2024 (36 KB; title “On the Goncharov's conjecture in degree m−1 and weight m”; abstract already states the same char-zero result). v2 17 Oct 2025 (46 KB; retitled). I did not diff the two bodies, so I cannot say whether scope changed. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.delivers: Goncharov's conjecture in the single degree i = m−1 (“next to Milnor”) for every weight m ≥ 2, over fields of characteristic zero, rationally. Includes m = 2 (Suslin's indecomposable K_3) and, for m = 3, degree 2 (K^{(3)}_4). Map is a quasi-isomorphism in general per Theorem 1.3 as read; it is stated as an isomorphism only over algebraically closed fields.
events.remains: Degrees 1 ≤ i ≤ m−2 for every m ≥ 3 (e.g. i = 1, 2 at weight 4); positive characteristic (author believes it extends, does not prove it); and the full conjecture for all fields, weights and degrees.

events.what_happened: Alexander Kupers, Daniil Rudenko and Ismael Sierra, “The Goncharov Lie coalgebra of a field” (arXiv:2606.23863, 129 pages). For an arbitrary field, defines a graded Lie coalgebra G(F) from E∞-homology of GL(F), gives a presentation, and constructs motivic and Hodge realisations. States Conjecture A.b for arbitrary F: K^{(n)}_{2n−i}(F)_Q ≅ H^i(G(F))_n for 1 ≤ i ≤ n. Theorem B for arbitrary F: K^{(3)}_4(F)_Q ≅ H^2(G(F))_3, and an exact sequence K^{(2)}_4(F)_Q ⊗ F^×_Q → K^{(3)}_5(F)_Q → H^1(G(F))_3 → 0. The paper says that for n = 3, Conjecture A.b “is equivalent to a conjecture of Goncharov [Gon95a, Conj 1.15]” about Γ_3(F;Q), and that Theorem B “affirms a variant of this conjecture”. It lists known cases of A.b, including (iii) i = n−1 by [Bol24]; items (i) and (ii) were not read.
events.revisions: v1 22 Jun 2026 only (145 KB on arXiv; 129 pages). No later version on the abstract page as of 2026-10-10.
events.delivers: For arbitrary fields, a weight-3 statement about G(F), not Γ(F,3): an isomorphism in degree 2 (K^{(3)}_4 ≅ H^2(G)_3), which the authors say is an instance of Bolbachan's result, and in degree 1 only an exact sequence identifying the indecomposable part of K^{(3)}_5 with H^1(G)_3. The authors call this a variant of Goncharov's weight-3 conjecture. The literal Γ_3 degree-1 statement is not claimed.
events.remains: The literal Γ_3 statement in degree 1 (only a variant and the indecomposable part are given); all weights n ≥ 4 for G(F) in degrees i < n−1 (for arbitrary fields); the general comparison between G(F) and Γ(F,n), which the paper does not establish beyond n = 3.
events.doubts: The authors' own wording is “variant”, not the literal conjecture. Their equivalence claim for n = 3 is stated in the text and I did not verify it against Gon95a Conj 1.15, which I could not access. Degree 1 is given only modulo decomposables. Very recent and 129 pages; no third-party reading found yet.
events.direction: Supports the conjecture in weight 3 in a variant form, with partial results for arbitrary fields. No counterexample.

events.what_happened: Kenichiro Kimura, “On a relation of a conjecture of Goncharov to the co-Lie algebra of Bloch–Kriz mixed Tate motives” (arXiv:2604.17671, 21 pages). Asks whether a linear map from Goncharov's group B_n(F) to the co-Lie algebra of the Bloch–Kriz category of mixed Tate motives can be defined via motivic polylogarithms. Gives supporting results under an assumption that part of the Beilinson–Soulé vanishing conjecture holds. A different question from Γ(F,n) cohomology: the target object is different.

events.direction: Conditional support for a neighbouring conjecture; neither proves nor disproves the cohomology statement; no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Kupers, Rudenko and Sierra, “Mixed Tate motives over number fields” (arXiv:2608.26392, 67 pages). For a number field F, Theorem A: a unique isomorphism of graded Lie coalgebras from G(F) to the motivic Lie coalgebra L^MTM(F) (the realisation map). Consequences the paper states: Corollary B proves the Goncharov universality conjecture for number fields, [Gon95b, Conjecture 17(a)] (every framed rational mixed Tate motive over a number field is a linear combination of motivic multiple polylogarithms); Corollary C on the kernel of the cobracket and a formula for ζ_F(n) up to a rational factor; the text says “Theorem A proves the above conjecture for F a number field”, i.e. Conjecture A.b of arXiv:2606.23863, for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n. For arbitrary fields, A.b is proved for i = n only (Lemma 3.1). The classical Zagier-type statement is conditional on the depth conjecture for G(F). The text read never mentions Γ(F,n).
events.revisions: v1 26 Aug 2026 only (80 KB on arXiv; 67 pages per comments).
events.delivers: For number fields only: the G(F)-version of the conjecture (Conjecture A.b, all n and all 1 ≤ i ≤ n, as the text says Theorem A proves it), and the Goncharov universality conjecture [Gon95b, Conj 17(a)], which is a different Goncharov conjecture about periods of mixed Tate motives. The step from G(F) to the Γ(F,n) statement is not made in this paper; KRS 2606 asserts the equivalence only for n = 3.
events.remains: The literal Γ(F,n) statement for number fields in weight n ≥ 4 (not addressed in the text read); arbitrary fields in degrees i < n (only i = n is proved); the Zagier-type classical statement (conditional).
events.direction: Supports the G(F)-version of the conjecture for number fields and proves the universality conjecture for number fields; no counterexample.

summary: Search (36 web queries, plus 20-odd page fetches) finds no resolution of Goncharov's conjecture on H^i(Γ(F,n)) since 26 January 2024, and no AI involvement in any source. Three in-window events move it, with different scope. (1) Bolbachan, arXiv:2404.06271 (v1 9 Apr 2024, v2 17 Oct 2025): for characteristic-zero fields and m ≥ 2, H^{m−1,m}(K,Q) ≅ H^{m−1}(Γ(K,m)). This is the next-to-Milnor degree for all weights. Theorem 1.3 calls the comparison map a quasi-isomorphism in general, an isomorphism over algebraically closed fields; I did not establish whether the quasi-isomorphism is degree-by-degree. No journal publication was found. (2) Kupers, Rudenko and Sierra, arXiv:2606.23863 (22 Jun 2026): for arbitrary fields they define G(F) and prove K^{(3)}_4(F)_Q ≅ H^2(G(F))_3, which they describe as an instance of Bolbachan's result, plus an exact sequence placing the indecomposable part of K^{(3)}_5 against H^1(G(F))_3. They say that for n = 3 their Conjecture A.b is equivalent to Goncharov's Conj 1.15 on Γ_3, and that Theorem B “affirms a variant”. (3) KRS, arXiv:2608.26392 (26 Aug 2026): for number fields, G(F) → L^MTM(F) is an isomorphism; the text says this proves Conjecture A.b for number fields, and proves the Goncharov universality conjecture [Gon95b, Conj 17(a)], which is a different question. The text never names Γ(F,n). KRS 2606 also treats Bolbachan's result as proving the i = n−1 case of A.b for every n, which is the closest the sources come to linking the G-version and the Γ-version beyond n = 3. Neighbouring events, discounted for scope: Kimura (Apr 2026, B_n(F) to Bloch–Kriz co-Lie algebra, conditional on Beilinson–Soulé), Aoki (Sep 2026, presentation of G(F)), Charlton (May 2024, Goncharov's depth conjecture in weight 6, depth 3). Pre-window neighbours: Rudenko (strong Suslin reciprocity, Compositio 2021), Bolbachan (2021, Chow dilogarithm), Gangl (2018, partial morphism in weight 4), Goncharov–Rudenko (first posted Mar 2018; Zagier at s = 4; weight-4 maps stated as Conjecture 1.4 and not proved in the text read; v5 of July 2026 says accepted by Annals). Talks (Radchenko June 2025; Kupers November 2025 Fields; Rudenko's colloquium) describe the KRS programme as work in progress and are not dated before the 2026 write-up, per §5.1. Close calls: whether Theorem B counts as the weight-3 Goncharov statement (the authors say no, a variant); whether Theorem A for number fields counts as the Γ-conjecture for number fields in weights ≥ 4 (the text does not say, and the equivalence is stated only at n = 3); whether Bolbachan's quasi-isomorphism covers every degree. AI: no source names an AI system. KRS 2606 acknowledges Steven Charlton for “computer-assisted methods” in its Section 7.3.3, which is computer assistance and not an AI system; Charlton's 2024 depth paper lists Mathematica worksheets as ancillary files. I searched for AI involvement with the problem's name and AI terms, plus the AI trackers and lab announcements that surfaced, and found only unrelated AI-math results (see search.dead_ends).
competing_reading: Read the 2026 KRS work as settling the conjecture in the cases that matter. Bolbachan's theorem gives the next-to-Milnor degree for all weights; KRS Theorem B gives weight 3 over arbitrary fields; KRS 2608 gives Conjecture A.b for number fields in all weights; and KRS state the A.b–Goncharov equivalence, and treat Bolbachan's result as proving A.b's i = n−1 case for every n, which suggests the G-version and the Γ-version coincide in general. On this reading the conjecture is essentially settled over number fields and in weight 3. The stronger reading against it: the authors call their weight-3 result a “variant”, state the equivalence only for n = 3, and never name Γ(F,n) in the number-field paper; the weight-4 maps are still stated as conjectures in Goncharov–Rudenko (in the rendering read); and Bolbachan covers only the single degree m−1. On this reading the conjecture is open except for specific degrees and weights, and the record should not be counted as resolved.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Goncharov 1995 (Adv. Math. 114), Conjecture 1.15 and Conjecture 1.1 as cited by Bolbachan, to fix whether the literal Γ_3 statement in degree 1 follows from KRS Theorem B. (2) Any statement in KRS 2608 or a later paper that H^i(Γ(F,n)) ≅ H^{i,n}_M(F,Q) for number fields and n ≥ 4, or a general comparison of G(F) with Γ(F,n). (3) The Annals (v5) text of Goncharov–Rudenko: whether Conjecture 1.4 (weight-4 maps are isomorphisms) is still conjectural or now proved. (4) Bolbachan v2 Theorem 1.3 in full, to settle whether the quasi-isomorphism gives the isomorphism in every degree. (5) Journal publication or named public refereeing of KRS 2606 and 2608 and of Bolbachan 2404.06271. (6) An expert survey or the Wikipedia article's status section, which the stub does not supply.
